newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Sulzer shares rocket on Medica plan.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sulzer shares rocket on Medica plan.

text.p: Swiss engineering group Sulzer AG sent its share price rocketing on Tuesday with plans to launch its profitable medical technology division Medica on the bourse in search of capital for acquisitions.
Registered shares closed 17 percent higher as investors cheered management's willingness to heed market calls for more transparency in the mixed industrial and medical conglomerate.
The registered shares added 144 francs to close at 982 and had jumped as high as 1,000 francs after Sulzer said it would offer about a quarter of the equity in Sulzer Medica around mid-year.
Chairman Pierre Borgeaud said the decision was a fundamental one and details remained to be worked out, including whether to list on one or more bourses in Europe or the United States.
"This was exactly the step that the market has long demanded," one Swiss exchange trader said.

Traders said the Medica flotation showed management was committed to restoring profits after two years of decline due to operating losses, one-time charges for restructuring, a U.S. patent dispute and an especially strong Swiss franc in 1995.

Net profit plunged 52 percent in 1995 to 92 million francs ($65 million) and was expected to be lower again for 1996, although chief executive Fritz Fahrni said the profit outlook for 1997 and beyond was positive.
Medica is a leading world supplier of orthopedic implants, cardiac pacemakers, mechanical heart valves and vascular grafts.

Sulzer's half-year 1996 report showed Medica operating profit up 14 percent at 191 million francs while losses at two of the four remaining industrial divisions dragged the overall result down to 173 million.
Sulzer's four industrial businesses are Rueti textile machinery and Infra building services, both lossmakers in the course of being turned around, along with Roteq pumps and Winterthur engineering.
It said the spin-off was part of a new duel growth strategy for the medical and industrial sectors agreed by the board of directors and executive management.
The industrial side would focus on internal growth while competition and conditions in the medical technology sector meant Medica needed the ability to make acquisitions.
"The planned initial public offering will provide this successful Sulzer group with the same access to capital resources as its main U.S. competitors," Sulzer said.
Chairman Borgeaud said analysts' figures for a Medica market capitalisation of around three billion francs were "a fair estimate".
But chief financial officer Erich Mueller said the exact value of Medica would have to be settled in talks with a bank that would be consulted on the public offering.
"In no way do I want to commit myself to a particular figure," Mueller said.
Sulzer has not yet decided on which bank should manage the public offering.
Mueller said firms like Medica generally traded at a price-earnings ratio of at least 25 or more. The three billion franc figure was based on that assumption. ($1=1.4141 Swiss Franc)
